reply_text:
I give this one **out**. The quote is on the page, but it is a statement about Facebook's business plans, not about what AI will do.

**Is the quote on the page?** Yes. I opened the Adweek page and the words appear exactly as quoted. The page is a news article by David Cohen titled "4Q EARNINGS CALL: Mark Zuckerberg Discusses Artificial Intelligence", from Adweek's paywalled Social Pro Daily section. It reprints a short excerpt from the earnings call. Zuckerberg was answering Colin Sebastian, an analyst at Robert W. Baird & Co., and the article is cut off by the paywall right after the excerpt. In full, the excerpt says: "Yann LeCun … joined us to lead our AI group. And this is a long-term research group that we have. It's going to fit into our strategy over a longer, maybe five- or 10-year period." The page's metadata gives a publication time of 2014-01-30T21:09. The article says the call was on "Wednesday", which matches 2014-01-29. This is coverage, not a transcript.

**The four parts of the rule:**
1. **Role: passes.** He was Facebook's founder and chief executive, and Facebook AI Research had started in 2013-12, about a month earlier.
2. **Looks forward and is about AI: fails.** The words say when a research group will fit into the company's strategy. That is a business or strategy forecast. They don't say AI will do, reach or ship anything, so they fall outside the rule's definition of a claim about AI. The search run's own note called it weak for the same reason. I don't read this as borderline.
3. **Date or length of time: passes.** "Maybe five- or 10-year period" is a span, so it would be due ten years on, around 2024.
4. **Primary source: coverage only.** As found, the source is the Adweek report. The call transcript itself would be the primary source, but I didn't fetch it.

**Already recorded?** No. None of his recorded files match this claim. The nearest, from 2018, is about AI detecting hate speech, which is a different claim.
